newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks sharply down amid rate concerns.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks sharply down amid rate concerns.

text.p: Mexican stocks were sharply down in late trade on Tuesday amid concern that primary interest rates would surge at a central bank auction to be held later in the day, traders and analysts said.
In the closing minutes of the session, the leading IPC share index was down 42.86 points, or 1.13 percent, at 3,753.06. Trading volume was moderate.
MMS Latin America situated an important support for the IPC at 3,750.28 points.
"Interest rates are on the way up, and dealers are bailing out of stocks," a desk trader said.

Banco de Mexico is expected to assign bellwether 28-day Cetes, or T-bills, at an average rate of 21.61 percent, up 302 basis points from its auction last week, according to a Reuters survey of eight money market traders in Mexico City.
